nodes.description: NTHL1 is the human homolog of Escherichia coli endonuclease III, a DNA glycosylase with associated AP-lyase activity that removes ring-saturated and ring-fragmented pyrimidines (thymine glycol, urea, 5-hydroxyuracil) to initiate base excision repair. Loss of NTHL1 leaves these lesions in DNA; 5-hydroxyuracil, an oxidation product of cytosine, is miscoding and templates C>T mutations. Other glycosylases (NEIL1, SMUG1, TDG, UNG2) also act on 5-hydroxyuracil, which may explain why the resulting mutation rate is only modestly raised; that explanation is an inference, not a tested claim.

nodes.description: Somatic cells of biallelic carriers accumulate C>T transitions at non-CpG sites, the pattern of COSMIC signature SBS30. The phenotype is a change in mutation type more than in mutation number: tumors are not hypermutated, and NTHL1-knockout human colon organoids accumulate base substitutions at about twice the normal rate with no increase in indels or structural variants. SBS30 is detectable at comparable proportions in adenomas and carcinomas, so it is present from the earliest neoplastic stage, and it dominates the somatic profile of tumors from several organs, which is the molecular argument that the extracolonic cancers belong to the syndrome rather than being coincidental. Somatic driver variants in APC, PIK3CA, TP53, PTEN, KRAS and NRAS, mostly C>T at non-CpG sites, were found in tumors from biallelic carriers.
